summary.name: HomelabOS
summary.one_liner: HomelabOS is an open-source, offline-first self-hosting platform that deploys and maintains over 100 services on your own servers.
use_cases: Replace cloud services like Gmail, Slack, and Google Drive
Back up data nightly with restic
Host services reachable over Tor without port forwarding
Run home services on a LAN while the internet is offline
Deploy and maintain a family or friends' server stack
summary.what_it_does: HomelabOS is a set of tools for deploying, backing up, restoring, and maintaining over 100 self-hosted applications, including video players, home automation, and chat services. It can configure services as Tor hidden services so they are reachable without a bastion server or port forwarding. It can use Terraform to deploy and configure a bastion server acting as a reverse proxy. Backups use restic nightly, and minio can back up to another server. Installation is done via a single bash install script from GitLab.
notable: Optional Tor hidden service configuration without port forwarding
Services keep running on LAN when external internet is offline
Terraform-based bastion server reverse proxy option
Nightly restic backups and minio backups to a friend's server
caveats: Page does not state the license beyond calling it free-as-in-speech; the awesome-selfhosted listing says MIT.
Platform support beyond Docker and a Linux install script is not explicitly stated on the page.
